**Step 1:** First, we write the inverse function implicitly. The given function is $y=2{x}^{5}+3{x}^{4}-{x}^{3}+6,$ and to write the inverse function implicitly, we swap $x$ and $y$ as follows:

$$
x=2{y}^{5}+3{y}^{4}-{y}^{3}+6
$$

Note that in the equation above, we have $y={h}^{-1}(x).$

**Step 2:** Next, we differentiate. The overall goal is to find $\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x},$ but the equation is already solved for $x,$ so we compute $\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}y}$ and then take the reciprocal:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}y} & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}y}(2{y}^{5}+3{y}^{4}-{y}^{3}+6) \\ \frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}y} & =10{y}^{4}+12{y}^{3}-3{y}^{2} \\ \frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =\frac{1}{10{y}^{4}+12{y}^{3}-3{y}^{2}}\end{aligned}
$$

**Step 3:** Lastly, we write the result in terms of ${h}^{-1}(x).$ Since $y={h}^{-1}(x),$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}[{h}^{-1}(x)] & =\frac{1}{10({h}^{-1}(x))^{4}+12({h}^{-1}(x))^{3}-3({h}^{-1}(x))^{2}} \\ {({h}^{-1})}^{′}(x) & =\frac{1}{10({h}^{-1}(x))^{4}+12({h}^{-1}(x))^{3}-3({h}^{-1}(x))^{2}}.\end{aligned}
$$
